screening_decisions.reason: RCT in women with stress urinary incontinence (USI). Includes PFMT arms (digital palpation and biofeedback) compared to a no-exercise control group. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT in women with SUI. The mobile app intervention resulted in 98.4% of participants performing PFMT at follow-up, making this essentially a PFMT delivery method. Control was postponed treatment (inactive). Meets selection criteria.
RCT in postmenopausal women with SUI. Includes PFME alone arm compared to control group. Biofeedback is an add-on, but PFME is the core intervention. Meets selection criteria.

RCT in women with urge and mixed UI. However, the intervention is 'biofeedback-assisted behavioral treatment' which is not clearly PFMT. The behavioral treatment may include bladder training and other components, but PFMT is not explicitly the primary intervention. Does not clearly meet the PFMT criterion.
RCT in older women with stress incontinence. Includes pelvic muscle exercise arm compared to control group. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with genuine stress incontinence. Includes PFMT arm compared to no treatment control. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized experimental study in women with SUI. Includes perineal exercises (PFMT) arm compared to control group. Meets selection criteria.
RCT in women with urodynamic stress UI. Includes PFMT arm compared to no treatment control. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with stress and mixed UI. Includes PFMT arm compared to control group. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with UI. BMP included pelvic floor muscle strength improvement as an outcome, suggesting PFMT is part of the intervention. Control was no treatment. Conservative decision to include.
Prospective randomized study in women with stress incontinence. 'Medical gymnastics' likely includes PFMT. Conservative decision to include due to unclear details in abstract.
RCT in elderly women with SUI. Intervention included exercises 'aimed at enhancing PFMs and fitness'. Control group present. Conservative decision to include as PFMT is part of intervention.
RCT in elderly women with stress, urge, and mixed UI. Exercise training likely includes PFMT components. Education group serves as inactive control. Conservative decision to include.
RCT in elderly women with stress, urge, and mixed UI. Multidimensional exercise treatment likely includes PFMT. Control group present. Conservative decision to include.

Controlled trial with random assignment in older women with heterogeneous UI. Intervention explicitly includes 'pelvic floor muscle training with manual palpation and verbal feedback'. Control received advice and educational pamphlet (inactive). Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with SUI. Includes PFMT arm compared to no treatment control. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with mild-to-moderate SUI. Intervention teaches timed PFMT ('The Knack'). Wait-listed control group. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with SUI. Includes PFMT arms (group and individual) compared to no treatment control. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in women with MUI. Includes PFMT arm compared to waiting list control. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT in postmenopausal women with UI. PT for UI likely includes PFMT as standard component. Control was osteoporosis education (inactive for UI). Conservative decision to include.
Study comparing bladder training vs pelvic muscle exercises in women with UI. Pelvic muscle exercise arm is PFMT. Control group mentioned. Meets selection criteria.
Experimental randomized study in women with SUI. Kinesitherapy (G2) likely includes PFMT. Control group present. Conservative decision to include.
Randomized experimental study in female volleyball athletes with SUI. PFMRP (pelvic floor muscles rehabilitation program) is PFMT. Control received pamphlet only. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized study in women with genuine stress incontinence. Includes pelvic floor exercises arm compared to control group. Meets selection criteria.
RCT in women with genuine stress incontinence. Includes PFMT arm compared to no therapy control. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating PFM training in women with stress or mixed UI vs untreated control group. Meets all criteria: RCT design, appropriate population (women with UI), PFMT intervention arm, and inactive control (no treatment).
RCT of nurse specialist involvement vs usual care for UI. Does not meet criteria: intervention is nurse practitioner involvement, not PFMT.
Satisfaction study assessing consumer views on nurse specialist care. Does not meet criteria: not an RCT testing PFMT intervention.

RCT of behavioral training (includes PFMT components) for urge incontinence in older women vs self-help booklet (inactive control). Meets criteria: RCT design, women with UUI, behavioral training intervention, inactive control.
Feasibility study of pelvic floor fitness program, not a proper RCT. Does not meet criteria: study design is feasibility study, not RCT.
RCT comparing intensive supervised vs unsupervised PFMT. Does not meet criteria: both arms receive active PFMT intervention, no inactive control group.
RCT of stabilization exercises focusing on PFMT vs routine physiotherapy. Does not meet criteria: control group receives active treatment (routine physiotherapy), not inactive control.

RCT of behavioral training (includes PFMT) with or without electrical stimulation vs self-help booklet (inactive control). Meets criteria: RCT design, women with stress incontinence, PFMT intervention, inactive control.
RCT of muscle strength training including Kegel's exercise vs control in long-term care facilities. Meets criteria: RCT design, women with UI, PFMT intervention (Kegel's), control group.
RCT of behavioral therapy for UI vs no therapy. Meets criteria: RCT design, women with UI, behavioral therapy intervention (likely includes PFMT), no treatment control.
RCT of internet-based PFMT program vs postal program vs no treatment. Meets criteria: RCT design, women with SUI, PFMT intervention, no treatment control arm available.
RCT comparing internet-based PFMT vs postal PFMT. Does not meet criteria: both arms receive active PFMT intervention, no inactive/no treatment control.
RCT comparing internet-based PFMT vs postal PFMT (follow-up). Does not meet criteria: both arms receive active PFMT intervention, no inactive/no treatment control.
RCT of TA and PFM co-contraction exercises vs control for SUI. Meets criteria: RCT design, women with SUI, PFMT intervention, control group.
RCT of behavioral UI treatments combined with physical activity vs control in frail older women. Meets criteria: RCT design, women with UI, behavioral intervention, control group.
RCT of PFRP (PFM training program) vs usual health care in gynecologic cancer survivors. Meets criteria: RCT design, women, PFMT intervention, usual care control (inactive for PFM).
Questionnaire validation study for ICIQ. Does not meet criteria: not an RCT, no PFMT intervention.

Systematic review of physical therapies for UUI. Does not meet criteria: not a primary RCT.
